Worst-case wire-time slowdown by budget and mean encoded record size `m`, from the closed form `slowdown = max(1, BDP × 4865 / (budget × (28 + m)))` at the specification bandwidth-delay product of 12.5 MB (1 Gbps × 100 ms and 100 Gbps × 1 ms coincide there): 4865 B is the pinned per-scope session envelope and 28 B the calibrated per-message wire cost beyond the record's encoded payload. A link's slowdown-1 crossover is `m* = BDP × 4865 / budget − 28`; the default row's, at the spec BDP, is m* ≈ 85.3 B. The factor prices the interleaved dispute walk only — supply runs stream outside the window — and costs latency, never memory: a session serializes into capacity-sized waves, deadlock-free at any budget. Cells are clamped at 1.0×, which is wire-time-optimal (bandwidth-bound stays bandwidth-bound); rows under a few MiB understate the true factor (the flat ~0.21 MB decode-fan pre-charge and the near-root band's full-fan scope prices both bite there).
